articleTitle: Electrical Signal Data Acquisition and Recording Customized System, with High Sampling Rate, for Data Analysis Optimization of Three-Phase Power Supply Consumers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Data acquisition and recording systems are very useful for monitoring industrial processes or electrical events in power plants, electrical signal analysis to reduce electricity consumption etc. This paper deals with a customized data acquisition and recording system for an electrical power cabinet that ensures the power supply of a three-phase consumer. The module for the acquisition, storage and transfer of the data related to monitored electrical signals performs the synchronous sampling of eight analog inputs (voltages and currents) with a high sampling frequency. The firmware of this module performs the synchronous sampling of the analog inputs, temporary data storage and their transfer into owner format compatible with specialized programs for analysis using Discrete Wavelet Transform or Fast Fourier Transform. The presented data acquisition and recording system has a Windows compatible associated software application which handles the equipment configuration, automatic transfer of the acquired data and their storage into a database available for other applications. The work focuses on software design, but also presents experimental results obtained using the presented data acquisition and recording customized system.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Control for Speed Sensor Failure in Induction Motor Drive based on Direct Torque Control and Adaptive Stator Flux Observer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: this paper deals with a speed sensor fault tolerant control (FTC) scheme for induction motor (IM) drive based on direct torque control (DTC) and adaptive stator flux observer (ASFO). Many important points are treated in the proposed algorithm, which are the detection of the sensor failure, isolation of the faulty sensor and the reconfiguration of the control system by proper estimation. An adaptive stator flux observer is used instead of classical flux and torque estimator to perform the stator flux components, electromagnetic torque, flux magnitude, rotor position and the estimated rotor speed. Furthermore, a fault detection and isolation (FDI) logic circuitry is used to detect speed sensor fault and isolate it and simultaneously generate a logic impulse to switch to the sensorless mode. The proposed algorithm is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Research on the Continuous Monitoring of the Sag of Overhead Electricity Transmission Cables Based on the Measurement of their Slope
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper present a proposed system for the continuous monitoring of conductor sag values in overhead electricity transmission lines through slope angle measurement, by using a mathematical model based on the catenary equation. By measuring the axial angle of the conductor and the slope angle by means of the double axis tilt sensor, the sag value can be calculated in case of cable swings. The results obtained according to the proposed algorithm developed in LabVIEW software environment showed that the system could meet the technical requirements for measuring conductor sag in electricity transmission lines.

articleTitle: Detection of electromagnetic emissions transmitted on the power line through electrical conduction
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper describes the process of detecting the signals representing the image shown on the video display of a laptop. There were selected several graphical images consisting in horizontal bars of various widths and the measurements were performed in two stages using two types of chargers for the laptop: a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) power supply and a shielded one,respectively. There are discussed the emission levels when using the shielded/COTS power supply, as well as the insertion loss of the electronic filter within the shielded power supply.

articleTitle: Testing Stand for Low-Power Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a modern stand for monitoring the operation of low-power electrical machines. There are presented the components of this stand and a monitoring program for the parameters of the tested machines. The program has been obtained by modifying, in LabVIEW, some modules of the original program delivered by the manufacturing company. Practically, any type of low-power electrical machines can be tested. The case of a single-phase asynchronous motor with auxiliary phase and starting capacitor is exemplified. The windows Metering, Oscilloscope, Phasor Analyzer and Harmonic Analyzer are presented for the case of supplying at 62 V (no-load operation) and 220 V (no-load operation and load operation). The paper ends with conclusions and references.

articleTitle: Indirect Current Control Algorithm Implementation for an Active Filtering System Using Constant Switching Frequency Hysteresis Controllers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is the implementation of a hysteresis current controller with constant switching frequency as a part of an active filtering system control algorithm, based on the indirect current control. The alternative in the literature to the hysteresis current controller is the PI controller that can give better overall performances and constant switching frequency but with the cost of comprehensive parameter tuning. A compromise can be achieved between the classical current controllers which is the hysteresis current controller with constant switching frequency. This can be obtained by combining the hysteresis comparators with the PWM suboptimal modulator. The obtained performances of the active filtering system based on the indirect current control are compared with the corresponding performances obtained by the same system implemented with the well documented PI current controller. The regulator implementation and performance comparative study were accomplished on a comprehensive active compensator system built in the Matlab Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Development of a wireless glove based on RFID Sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Sensor gloves are devices used to implement interfaces for human-machine interactions which are utilized in a wide range of applications such as control of embedded systems, translation of sign language, gestures recognition, medical rehabilitation etc. This paper presents a wireless sensor glove based on the use of RFID sensors. For this type of sensors, the energy supplied for measurement and for the communication of measured data back to the reader is provided exclusively by the reader via the electromagnetic field. Therefore, it was important for the device to be designed so that the power consumption be minimal. For this reason, our sensor glove is designed using devices capable of harvesting the electromagnetic energy from the reader, monitor this energy and consume it only when needed by using a microcontroller which features several very low power consumption modes.

articleTitle: On Automatic Transfer Switch System Security
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents an automatic transfer switch system that ensures a secure power system by integrating advanced digital functions with the notions of Internet Of Things (IoT), connectivity and resiliency. There are presented the power systems vulnerabilities followed by a practical study case of an in the house built secure automatic transfer switch system (ATSS) by addressing the cyber-attack which can take place on the transmission command of the ATSS. The remote monitoring and control modules (transmitter and receiver units) are also presented along with a detailed description of the encoding algorithm.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Train Operation using Simulated Annealing Algorithm and SIMULINK model
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient algorithm starting from the mathematical model of the train motion. Using the mathematical model it is created the SIMULINK model of the train motion. By using the Simulated Annealing Algorithm it is determined the minimum value of the energy consumed by the electric train for a specified route.

articleTitle: Design Analysis of a Permanent Magnet Brushless Generator with Two Counter Rotating Rotors for Small-Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic behavior of a Permanent Magnet Brushless Generator developed for a small-wind energy conversion system. The generator has two counter-rotating rotors direct-driven by two Darrieus turbines in opposite directions. The electromagnetic design and optimization analysis are carried out by means of finite-element magnetic-field analysis. This paper presents simulation results to establish the generator's performance.

articleTitle: Occupational Exposure to Power Frequency Magnetic Fields in Intensive Care Unit Rooms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Current intensive care unit rooms have many medical devices. Typically, this type of equipment produces low frequency magnetic field. As a result, staff and patients are permanently exposed to magnetic fields of different intensities. The effects of magnetic field on human health have not yet been clearly confirmed. In occupational environments, the exposure to magnetic field of industrial frequency is recognized as a hazard factor for a range of disturbances. The objective of this work is to describe exposure to magnetic fields of industrial frequency in intensive care unit rooms at Al- Kadhimiya Hospital in Baghdad, through a series of measurements in the environment where medical personnel perform their daily professional activities and patients must remain for several hours or days. The results indicate the following: · The predominant frequency in the intensive care unit rooms was 50 Hz. · The exposure levels obtained from the abovementioned monitoring process ranged from 0.33 to 4.44 mG in the intensive care unit rooms. · Getting the best information on the level of exposure of a specific person working in a specific environment is done through instantaneous environmental measurements. · The magnetic field density in intensive care unit rooms depends on the number and type of monitors and medical equipment which is used in those rooms.

articleTitle: On the energy efficiency of standalone fuel cell/renewable hybrid power sources Part I: Simulation results for constant load profile without RES power
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper it is proposed a Hybrid Power Source (HPS), based on Renewable Energy Sources (RES), and a Fuel Cell (FC) system as backup energy source, which uses an optimal control strategy for the fueling rates of the FC (hydrogen and air) based on the load following (LF) control. The RESs power profile is given by the Photovoltaic (PV) panels and Wind Turbine (WT). The power architecture is implemented and simulated in Matlab -Simulink ® environment. Hydrogen and air needed to sustain the load are achieved through the LF reference current generated in the LF control loop. This LF reference current will control the hydrogen flow rate (Fuel) or the air flow rate (AirFr) via the FuelFr and AirFr regulators considering the two topologies proposed here: Air-LF topology and Fuel-LF topology. In the first HPS topology, the air flow is controlled by AirFr regulator, the regulator being controlled by the LF controller. In the second configuration the hydrogen flow is controlled by the FuelFr regulator, the regulator being also controlled by the controller LF. The ESC optimization of the FC electrical energy efficiency and the total fuel consumption will be implemented here to find the global maximum of the multimodal optimization function defined here as the FC net power. The performance for these HPS topologies are compared for constant load profile without RES power, an in part two of the paper for variable load profile with different renewable energy sources profiles (RES) based on the following indicators: fuel consumption efficiency (Fuel<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub>), FC net power and total fuel consumption (Fuel<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>).

articleTitle: On the energy efficiency of standalone fuel cell/renewable hybrid power sources Part II: Simulation results for variable load profile with different renewable energy sources profiles (RES)
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the first part of the paper two proposed topologies are compared for constant load profile without Renewable Energy Sources (RES) power. The performance for these Hybrid Power Source (HPS) topologies are compared based on the following indicators: fuel consumption efficiency (Fuel<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub>), FC net power and total fuel consumption (Fuel<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>). The second part of the paper presents the simulation results for variable load profile with different renewable energy sources profiles (RES). As well as in the first part of the paper, the Extremum Seeking Control (ESC) optimization of the Fuel Cell (FC) electrical energy efficiency and the total fuel consumption will be implemented here to find the global maximum of the multimodal optimization function defined here as the FC net power. The load dynamic profile for both topologies (Air-LF, Fuel-LF) is set using the following sequence of the load currents: time sequence [s]: [0 2 3 8 9 10 10.5 12] and the sequence of the load currents [A]: [14 14 29 29 -6.5 -6.5 29 29]. The RESs power profile it is obtained using photovoltaic panels and wind turbines, for a sunny day with clouds and moderate wind during the evening. The performance for these HPS topologies are compared for variable load profile with different renewable energy sources profiles (RES) based on the following indicators: fuel consumption efficiency (Fuel<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub>), FC net power and total fuel consumption (Fuel<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>). The power architecture is implemented and simulated in Matlab-Simulink ® environment.

articleTitle: On-line Electrical Parameters Estimation of an Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The article presents a new method for on-line estimating the electrical parameters of an induction motor. In this regard, a Luenberger observer is used, which is online adapted according to the estimated electrical parameters. The stator and rotor resistance, stator inductance as well as dispersion coefficient are estimated based on some adaptive methods. The estimation method is tested and validated by simulation in Matlab-Simulink.

articleTitle: AC Resistance of Inductive Coupler with Pitch Coils for Contactless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In recent years, many results in the field of contactless power transfer by inductive coupling have been published. Practical applications start from very low delivered powers of a few mW in case of medical implants, up to powers of the order of kW in case of charging the electric vehicle (EV) batteries. The key element of the power transfer system is the inductive coupler made of two planar coils of certain (circular or rectangular) shape, located at variable distances from one another. In this paper there are analyzed the inductive couplers used at EV, for transferred powers of kW or tens of kW, with a view to increasing the power transfer efficiency. An efficient design of the inductive coupler may be done only by knowing its parameters in the frequency range in which the system operation is provided.

articleTitle: Design evaluation of several electric machines topologies for propulsion of a railway vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper approaches the electromagnetic design and finite-element analysis of two outer rotor machines topologies: radial flux NdFeB permanent magnet synchronous machines and asynchronous machine. The design evaluation of the machines, based on 2-D finite element field analysis, proves that using bonded NdFeB permanent magnets the efficiency of the machine is increased with the penalty of higher costs, due to high price of magnets. Induction machine has the energy conversion efficiency, especially at nominal power, approximately the same. The benefits of the asynchronous machine compared to permanent magnet variants are: lower production costs, higher operating temperature, better robustness, and disadvantages: lower power density, lower power factor.

articleTitle: Power Quality Analysis System Based on LabVIEW Real-Time and Reconfigurable FPGA Modules Using Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper present a Quality (PQ) monitoring system for the purpose of detection of PQ disturbances using Wavelet Transform (WT). The proposed system is based on the real-time capabilities of the Real-Time LabVIEW operating system and on a CompactRIO type realtime computer which contains a network of FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array). The WT is used to analyze the quality of energy and to detect the transient phenomena characteristic of the quasi-periodic signals. The system achieves the storage of entries as TDMS (Technical Data Management Streaming) files and Word/Excel type automatic reports automatically sent by email at predefined addresses, contains an OPC UA (Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture) type server for communication with a hierarchically superior SCADA (Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition) type system, performs selective entry of the characteristic parameters into a database, contains a Webserver for Intranet/Internet access, for viewing the measured data, and for system management from anywhere, the application is connected to a Cloud-type platform. The PQ monitoring system has been tested using both simulated signals and real signals from a practical experiment.

articleTitle: Simulink Model for Resistive Tubular Heater
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a model developed on the Matlab-Simulink platform for a resistive tube heating element. The proposed Simulink model is based on the mathematical model, the concept of which was presented in detail in a previously published work. It has been designed so that it can be easily adapted to various situations where the heating elements in tube are immersed in liquids or embedded in solid materials. One concern was to minimize the parameters that need to be pre-calculated based on physical, constructive data, in order to enroll them in the prescription blocks of the model. The viability of the modeling system presented was verified both by comparison with a real heating element and by drawing the temperature curves that highlight the fitting in the temperature differences internally admitted for such an element.

articleTitle: Smart Meters, PMU and PQ data analysis in Active Distribution Grids – Case Studies in MV networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Due to high renewables penetration, Active Distribution Networks are becoming a reality for every DSO. During previous years sustained effort was spent to accommodate the distribution network operational requirements to new challenges. Some topics about the DER impact on MV distribution network such as unwanted islanded operation or optimal penetration degree were covered in various studies. This paper continues the analysis of the Active Distribution Networks challenges in a case study with three micro hydroelectric power plants connected to a medium voltage distribution network. The analysis is focusing on the use of new smart meter design and of new phasor measurement unit (PMU) and power quality analyzers, in order to perform necessary observability and to enable new strategies needed to optimize the network operation or to detect and perform islanding measures in the case of networks with high renewable penetration.

articleTitle: Impact of the Stator Short-circuit, Rotor Broken Bar and Eccentricity Faults on Rotor Force for Loaded and No-load Induction Motors Operation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Based on finite element analysis in time domain of a squirrel cage induction motor this paper studies the influence of the three faults - stator short-circuit, broken rotor bar and static eccentricity on the mean values and harmonics of the rotor unbalanced force. Results for loaded motor operation and for no-load motor operation are compared. The healthy state of motor operation and seven faulty cases, with single, double and triple faults, are considered. All faulty cases are characterized by important increase of the rotor force compared with the healthy case.

articleTitle: Selection of the Power Components for a Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge Converter with Current Doubler
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper a method for selection of power components based on mathematical derivation of currents and voltages equations is presented. The key benefit is very practical and it can be easily implemented in engineering math software (e.g. Mathcad). This method is applied for selection of components for a Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge converter with current doubler. This approach could be used for other type of converters if is correctly adapted. Simulations are performed to prove the consistency of the results.

articleTitle: New Analysis Regarding Electromagnetic Field Emissions of a Wireless Device
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The rapid development of IT technologies, the apparition of internet, diverse social networks, the increase of online transmission and data in time along with video images, has led to the achievement of new modern, performant equipment which meet these actual requirements. Together with these achievements, interdisciplinary researches have also begun regarding the determination of electromagnetic field emissions of these devices along with their short-term, average and long-term effects over the human health.Within this article, the results of some recent experimental determination have been presented in terms of electromagnetic field emissions for a router type AC750 Dual Band, 750 Mbps, 2.4 GHz frequently used to connect to the internet in homes, offices, campuses etc. The measurements have been performed in the Electromagnetic Compatibility Laboratory within National Institute for Research Development and Testing in Electrical Engineering of Craiova - ICMET using the latest and most modern equipment (a dipole antenna of PCD-8250 type precision manufactured by the company ARC SEIBERSDORF and a spectrum analyser type Anritsu Spectrum Master MS 2711D). The experimental results have underlined that the electromagnetic field emission values are within the accepted limit currently regulated.

articleTitle: The influence of neutral treatment system type on the efficiency / performance of the MV networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims to presents an analysis of the performance and efficiency of the neutral system treatment type from an electrical power substation 110kV / MV which belongs to Energy Distribution Oltenia DEO depending on the level of active and reactive power losses from each case. All these were analyzed in two major conditions in terms of operating mode, namely: in normal operating mode and in fault mode, for two situations concerning the neutral treatment type: first when the neutral treatment system is done by an suppresion coil connected straight to the internal services power transformer and the second one when the neutral treatment is realized by a resistor connected to the system via a special equipment used to do an artificial neutral point. As a conclusion it is found that the type of the neutral system treatment is very important from the technical point of view and in the same time it directly influence also the cost efficiency of the power distribution by the level power losses.

articleTitle: Analogue flow control of a network of centrifugal air compressors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The air installation consists of a main pipe in which 10 high-capacity centrifugal compressors pump air simultaneously. The overall air flow rate of the compressors that pump in the same pipe can be regulated through the actuation of the air suction valve of each compressor. By closing or opening the suction valve, the flow rate of each compressor can be regulated, thus enabling the control of the overall flow. From a central electronic cabinet, an analogue command is given to each compressor's suction valve. This one responds with an analogue feedback on the flow rate of the compressor. If there are two types of compressors within the plant, the automated control allows closing or opening the suction valves in a certain order. Thus, besides the primary objective to ensure a certain flow, high energy efficiency is also attained.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of a Flyback Converter with Different Magnetic Media, for Micro-Power Controllers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study presents the numerical modelling of a miniature, planar, power transformer (PT) used in flyback convertors for low-power applications. The magnetic circuit is built using ferrite and magnetic nanofluid media. The converter is powered by a pulse width modulated voltage (PWM) supply. The PT is provided with an air-gap in the central column of the ferrite core. This paper is concerned with the discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) in addition to the high frequency operation mode of the device. The magnetic circuit is sized to minimize losses during the switching time. Thermal stability of the device is also considered.

articleTitle: Experimental Installation of Photovoltaic MPPT Controller Using Arduino Board
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Nowadays, several electronic devices as field programmable gate arrays (FPGA) and dSPACE controllers are used to implement the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for the photovoltaic (PV) systems applications. In contrast, the PIC microcontrollers are recommended to be used due to its low cost and simplicity compared with the other hardware devices. In this paper, the Arduino microcontroller is used to validate the function of perturb and observe (P&O) MPPT controller used with a stand-alone PV system under constant climate conditions and step variations in the connected load. From the comparison of experimental and simulation results, the available maximum power of the solar panel is successfully extracted by using Arduino Uno board irrespective of the variable load conditions.

articleTitle: Engine Speed Control Unit for an Aircraft Jet Engine with Coolant Injection into the Combustor
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper deals with an aircraft single jet turbo engine with coolant injection into its combustion chamber. In order to improve the engine's behavior, the coolant injection system (CIS) was correlated to the fuel control unit (FCU) of the engine, so it has result a new engine speed controller. The correlation valve was modeled starting from its non-linear equations, then brought to a linear dimensionless form and was added to the embedded system model, described by its block diagram with transfer functions. The embedded system (engine+ FCU+ CIS) quality was evaluated by studying its time behavior (some Simulink-Matlab simulations were performed), considering as single input the power lever angle (PLA), comparing system's behavior with and without correlation. Quantitative determinations are based on previous research results developed in Aerospace Engineering Laboratories in University of Craiova and on existing aircraft engines models (taken from technical scientific literature and author's previous contributions).

articleTitle: Modeling Three-Phase Short-Circuits in Grids Connected to Windfarms
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Monitoring windfarms in short-circuit conditions represents a quite important issue of electric power networks supplied by renewable sources. The method presented in the paper aims to establish in laboratory conditions, using the similitude criteria, the real value and the duration of a three phase short-circuit current acting in windfarms connected to the electric grids. Consequently, the paper presents the modeling of a real grid, in order to emulate, as accurate as possible. The results of the measurements, reported to the real grid, represent the real one, existing at the three phase short-circuit level. Therefore, even from the early design phase, one may choose the breaking equipment, capable to face the conditions of dynamic and thermal stability.

articleTitle: Synthesis of the Battery Charging System of a Stand-Alone Electric Locomotive Using the Traction Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents the synthesis of the battery charging system of an electric stand-alone locomotive. The traction converter as boost rectifier is used together with a dedicated control strategy in order to obtain the unity power factor on the grid. Next, the entire system is analyzed under Simulink environment and the energetic performances are determined.

articleTitle: On Feedback Controlling of a Smooth Version of Chua Dynamical System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper takes into account the smooth version of the Chua's dynamical system. The aim is to approach the state-space linearization and find an appropriate control u for the model. The results will be further used to find the global non-linear controller form of the dynamical system.

articleTitle: Use of Numerical Methods in Computation of Operation Characteristics for Brushless Direct Current Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Researches regarding use of brushless direct current motors in driving light conveyances(scooters, bicycles, motor-scooters), are present owing to their simple construction and low consumption of electrical energy. The study carried out and the simulations presented aim at presenting a mathematical model used for determining the operation characteristics, necessary in increasing the exigencies of the driving system. To be noted that the errors between the simulated characteristics and the experimental ones do not exceed 3.55%, thatjustifies the opportunity of the research.

articleTitle: Automatic sorting and handling system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Applications based on robotic handling solve many problems in different areas, especially in the food, pharmaceutical, plastics, building materials, or logistics applications. The paper presents an automatic electropneumatic system for manipulation and sorting of parts according to color. The system is taught to sort two kinds of pieces, both white and black. Pieces of different types arrive at the input stock and are picked up by a manipulating robot, then stored in two output stocks according to color.

articleTitle: Fast movements and jerk mechanics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study some extended fast motions, determined by the third order Euclidean Lagrangian. We consider some dynamic situations determined by initial non-null conditions that ends in null speed and acceleration. The subject is topical because we model a less studied type of movements that can lead to interesting new developments.

articleTitle: Small wind turbine selection for urban environment operation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In future Smart cities, renewable energy sources (RES) based microgrids (MGs) with energy storage facilities will be the main source for powering electric vehicles (EVs) based transportation systems. A residential charging station, supplied by renewable energy sources like wind and photovoltaic is considered in the present study. The main focus is on determining which small wind turbine is more suitable to complement a PV system in an urban EV charging station. Simulations using Homer software are performed to yield the most appropriate wind turbine for the particular location.

articleTitle: The Analyze of the Electrical Energy Production in Romania by Categories of Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: rotors; power transformers; machine control; induction motors; power engineering computing; finite element analysis; renewable energy sources; power grids; photovoltaic power systems; power convertors.

articleTitle: A Note on the Behavior of the Lü Dynamical System in a Slightly Simplified Version
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In the present note we make a study of the dynamics of Lü's system, using the appropiate Hamilton-Poisson structure and using the software for mathematics MAPLE 15. It will be analyzed the phase portrait for two particular simplified versions of the dynamical system associated to the Lü ordinary differential system.

articleTitle: A new approach to determine heat transfer coefficient of crimped connections
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The main goal of this paper was to use a mathematical model in order to calculate the heat transfer coefficient corresponding to crimped connections. The research started from an experimental determination of crimped connection temperature by heating a sample until steady state regime was reached. There were considered different values of A.C. current. Starting from experimental values, it was calculated the heat transfer coefficient corresponding to 510 A, 680 A, 850 A and 1110 A. Then, it was developed a coupled numerical model - A.C. Magnetic -- Steady State Heat Transfer in QuickField Professional, which uses heat transfer coefficient in order to estimate the steady state temperature. As it can be seen from experimental and numerical results the differences between two approaches are extremely high (from 51.6 % up to 68.9 %). It can be possible to increase the efficiency of this approach by using iteration and finding the right values of heat transfer coefficient. So, this study could be a starting point to a new research for determining heat transfer coefficient value using a method based on iteration which involves modifying $h _{\Sigma }$ value in numerical model until the experimental temperature steady state value is reached.

articleTitle: Calculation of Surges Transmitted Between Transformer Windings Using the Coupled Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a calculation method for voltage transmitted between the windings of the transformer while it is being subjected to the lightning impulse using the coupled circuit model; it describes the reasoning and analytical relations for determination of the electrical and magnetics parameters that influence the transmitted voltage between the windings of the transformer. The study was conducted on a 40MVA, 123/6.3 kV transformer, without adjustable winding, and the results achieved by calculation have been validated through experimental mesurements.

articleTitle: Integrated System of Water Engineering for Smart Residences
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to propose a gap analysis aimed to develop an integrated system that allows efficient water management in a residential space, displaying and retrieving relevant information requested by consumer, buildings administrators, water operators, stakeholders and decision making factors. The system must encourage the citizen and the decision making factors to promote an efficient water management in an area or in the built environment, taken account that, as an important resource, the water could become “smart” through the instrumentality of the systems of collecting, cleaning, measuring and monitoring. A smart water technology in a built environment allows seeing the efficiency of the distribution system and the real time consumption. In terms of finding an alternative source of water, a valuable resource is the rainwater. The usage of the rainwater can reduce the water bills and provide an alternative supply during water restrictions. Better collection of the rainwater would decrease the rainwater runoff and would reduce local flooding.

articleTitle: Studies on the cooling systems for the production of electricity through Seebeck effect with TEG elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims the presentation of studies on the use of different variants of cooling systems for the production of electrical energy by Seebeck effect with TEG cells. There are presented a number of 4 variants of electricity production systems with TEG elements, in simple circuit or placed in series where the cooling systems are either with fan operated or with liquid type glycol. There are determined experimentally the variations and the evolution in time of the process parameters, the temperatures and the electrical voltage produced in the conditions of the use of real-time command s and control systems.

articleTitle: Computer Assisted Equipment Selection for Components of Electric Panels
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this work we present a specialized software that should be used in the bidding or design phases for the optimal choice of the equipment that make up the automatic switching system from the base source to the backup source. The use of the software does neither require wide electric engineering knowledge, design knowledge nor electric circuit sizing know-how, and can be used by the bidding and supply staff. The advantage of using this software is the possibility to quickly select the necessary technical equipment in order to obtain a technically competitive automation system at a convenient price. The software we propose in this work is based on sizing calculations and predefined lists of standardized equipment provided by various producers and suppliers. Upon inputting variable values, the software outputs a price estimate and a list of electric gear, including the life-size equipment dimensions. The software application allows the sales engineer to draw up the necessary documentation, without the assistance of the design engineer, in order to establish a correct price estimate.

articleTitle: Testing Digital Relays through Secondary Currents Injection
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Protecting the electric power systems represents one of the major problems aiming to assure the stability and the continuity of the supply with electrical energy. The development of the protection systems using digital relays imposes an innovative approach concerning the testing, the setting of these relays along with a staff specialized in their firmware. Since, due to the high values of the short-circuit currents it is difficult to test the operation of the relays in situ, for instance in transformer stations or substations, it is mandatory to test and set the digital relays using the injection of secondary currents. The paper presents both the testing procedure that uses special devices for the secondary currents injection along with the test on models obtained from the real grids using the similitude criteria. Since the reporting factors are known, along with the possibility of using the accurate reported value of the real short-circuit current on the model, the tests on model present advantages in relation to the use of the devices of secondary currents injection. The results of the measurements on the model confirm the viability of the last testing method here depicted.

articleTitle: Using Numerical Methods for Establishing the Performances of Low Power Asynchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The opportunity of this work is backed by the possibility to predetermine the operating characteristics of the asynchronous motor in the rated regime, and thus by the possibility of constructing a high performance electric drive.The motors consume a lot of electrical energy, leading to an increase in the operational cost, if run for a long time. Due to its robustness, good power/mass ratio and ease of maintenance, the asynchronous motor is widely used in industry. Qualitative and quantitative predetermination of dynamic processes related to the field of use led to major investments and extensive research in large laboratories. Research on an asynchronous motor with a power of 1.5 kW, with variable parameters, proved that between the simulated and the experimentally determined values, the errors do not exceed 3%. There is a methodical approach for obtaining the values necessary in the design process of the motor used in the drive system of a multiple unit electric train. Simulation waveforms were generated using Mathcad software package, while some preliminary results are provided for a laboratory prototype. The results support the research carried out, providing simulations in compliance with the actual standards for the rated regime. The method is easy to deploy for low-power, fast-response, ripple-free electric drives, delivering greater power savings with respect to the output power, compared with previous research.

articleTitle: Powertrain 48V Power Supply Proposal and Safety Validation Voltage Levels for BLDC Motor Driver ASIC
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a design proposal for 48V power supply for a BLDC (Brushless Direct Current) motor driver chip. The BLDC actuator is used in 48 V mild hybrid Powertrain in target applications such starter generator or electric oil pump where the safety is very relevant. The focus is set on the design experience faced during testing the required voltage levels for BLDC driver ASIC (application specific integrated circuit): 48V, 12V, 5V and 3V3. The performance in terms of normal functioning, under-voltage (UV) and overvoltage (OV) has been investigated and validated by the experimental activities. Furthermore, the FTTIs (Fault Tolerant Time Intervals) were monitored in order to give evidence that the safety mechanism successfully avoid violation of proper functioning of the BLDC actuator. In case of safety relevant faults such OV or UV, the BLDC driver has to achieve a safe state within FTTI. There are two safe states available: the BLDC driver will put the inverter in high impedance or the inverter will be driven to break the motor.

articleTitle: Human-Machine Interfaces for Robotic System Control
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper reveals the design and development, from the concept to the experimental model, of a hardware and software of a rehabilitation robotic system, as well as the development of the human-machine interface necessary for the easy control of the robotic system. The resulting human-machine interfaces, developed on a dedicated HMI unit, are simple, intuitive and easy to use, offer the feeling that the therapists can fully and comfortably exploit all the resources of the robotic system. The rehabilitation robotic system is a fully functional experimental model and it presents a number of advantages for patients.

articleTitle: On Currents Asymmetry Protection For Three Phase Low Voltage Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The article presents an analysis of asymmetric currents protections for general-purpose three-phase low voltage induction motors. Dedicated electronic protection is provided to detect currents asymmetry on the motor phases. An electronic asymmetry protection with Hall transducers, AC current to DC voltage electronic module, low capacity PLC, and motor's power contactor has been developed. Experiments with industrial electronic asymmetry protection, an electronic module and FBD program for PLC of the proposed protection that are used for currents asymmetric protection are presented.

articleTitle: Study of Dynamic Stability a Cannard Configuartion UAV
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) having no pilots have proven their values in many areas. In this research we have made an attempt to design and analyze an indigenous UAV in terms of dynamic stability, knowing the mass of the entire system. Both lateral and longitudinal stability analysis of the UAV have been carried out at different conditions such as different airplane geometry and mass so that the best results are extracted. The stability analysis has been carried out in XFLR 5 software. The flight machine used in this analysis is a Canard Configuration UAV designed to operate at low Reynold numbers. The results of this analysis could be utilized to further improve the aerodynamics of the existing design and enhance the stability and performance characteristics of the UAV.

articleTitle: On the AC-Connecting of a System for Active Filtering and Regeneration in Active DC-Traction Substations
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach in the AC-connection filter design of a shunt active power filter based on three-phase voltage source inverter. The practical case study is of a LCL passive filter with damping resistors connected to the output of the inverter in an active DC-traction substation with 12-pulse parallel diode rectifier. Starting from the functions to be fulfilled, the design conditions are based on the transfer function related to the input and output currents. They consist of imposing the magnitude response at the switching frequency, as well as the position of the resonance frequency relative to the frequency of the highest order harmonic to be compensated. The design algorithm is fully formulated, some limitations are expressed and specific performance indicators are proposed. Through simulation in Matlab-Simulink environment, the proper operation of the whole system, including the designed interface filter, is illustrated.

articleTitle: Diagnosis with Analytic Model of a Rectifier for Faults on the Load Side
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The diagnosis of the electric systems is an actual item for the specialists in domain. Due to the variety of the measurements and multiplicity of faults which can be analyzed, the approach is motivating. The model reproduces the behavior of a system both in normal operation and fault occurrence. The procedure which uses the analytic models compares the system evolution in normal and fault conditions operation. Authors had previously studied different faults within a controlled rectifier-DC motor system. The paper deals with the analysis of a fault on the load side and its effects on the rectifier operation.

articleTitle: About Pathologic Linear Circuits With Inconsistent Initial Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a procedure for the regularization of the inconsistent initial conditions in linear electrical circuits, which contain loops consisting of independent and/or controlled voltage sources and capacitors, or cut-sets of independent and/or controlled current sources and inductors. Modeling of switched circuits by idealized models of switches have often led to discontinuities of circuit variables at the time instances of switching, phenomena called as inconsistent initial conditions. In these cases, Dirac impulses and their various order derivatives can occur in the expressions of the capacitor currents and inductor voltages, which are proportional to the derivatives of the discontinuous variables (charges/voltages, and fluxes/currents respectively). Because of these impulses, the inconsistent initial conditions at t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0-</sub> are converted into consistent initial conditions at t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0+</sub>. In this paper we present a simple method for the analysis of complex switched circuits that solves this problem.

articleTitle: Brush Lifting Systems for Wound Rotor Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The industrial processing equipment operates with high starting torque due to inertial load. Typically, these applications use wound rotor induction motors. To ensure a high starting torque for a limited input current, these motors are started with a rheostat connected with the rotor winding. The paper presents for the first time a new system for short-circuiting the rotor windings and brush lifting (BLD) developed at ICMET Craiova. The paper also addresses the key design challenges and the reliability requirements which these systems must meet.

articleTitle: LED and Incandescence Lamps in Railroad Repetitive Light Signals: A Comparative Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this work we study the efficiency of LED light sources compared to the incandescence light sources used in repetitive light signals of railroad traffic safety installations. For the two light sources we determined the luminous flux values, the energy efficiency and the illumination, in laboratory conditions. Afterwards we made field measures on locations where repetitive light signals are installed with the two types of light sources. Our results show that it is necessary to find resources and design solutions to replace the glowing light bulbs with LED ones for all luminous components of traffic safety installations.

articleTitle: Designing a Graphical User Interface with Matlab to select the ideal covering coefficient of the polar pitch for a salient pole synchronous generator calculation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper treats aspects of the geometrical design of salient synchronous generator. It focus on the transformation of given experimental data maps into polynomial based regression model. The aim of this work is to summarize many specific recommendations about details of implementation and design a Graphical User Interface with which, the user perform a specific task in area of designing a salient synchronous generator. The proposed task for this paper is to interpolate and to plot the dependence between ideal covering coefficient of the polar pitch and real one, based on the curves offered by the literature. Using this representation, the user/the designer could choose the appropriate value of the ideal covering coefficient of the polar pitch for its case study in a short time and, also, could send this data to the main program. The added value of this work is to create a tool which could be used easier, in different situations. This tool is a part of a collection of graphical user interfaces used in a computer aided design of a pole synchronous generator calculation.

Author Keywords: ideal covering coefficient of the polar pitch
real covering coefficient of the polar pitch

articleTitle: Dynamic Operation of High Power Synchronous Generator in Asynchronous Regime or encountering Three-Phase Shortcircuit
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a method of modeling the synchronous machine subjected to transient regimes. Then, the obtained model is utilized to simulate the dynamic behavior of the high power synchronous generator in conditions of asynchronous operation and for sudden three-phase short circuit occurred at the stator winding terminals. The model is based on Park-Blondel equations expressed in canonical form. The equations are built considering the influence of the induced current into the massive rotor of the generator and the nonlinearity of the magnetization characteristic. For the fulfillment of the simulated cases, an implicit Gear algorithm of third order is applied for the integration of the equations. The results obtained through simulations performed using the proposed model, are compared to those obtained running the predefined model offered for the synchronous machine by Simulink package from MATLAB. In both cases identical simulation scenarios are considered.

articleTitle: Studies on the determination of process parameter variation at dry monodisc braking
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims at presenting some studies regarding the determination of the variation of some functional parameters in disk braking, in the conditions of the torque and speed changes, corresponding to the braking of the vehicles on dry road. The experimental determination of the braking process parameters is made by measuring them on an experimental stand and analyzing the interdependencies between them. The speed, braking torque and temperatures inside the brake pads are measured, recorded and analyzed with specific sensors.

articleTitle: Assesment of the Near Field Level in the Vicinity of an Inverted V Antenna used for HF emission
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims to analyze the electromagnetic field components in the near field of a high frequency (HF) emission antenna. The typical case of a dipole antenna emitting Near Vertical Incident Skywave (NVIS) HF signals at two emitting frequencies (3.6 MHz and 7.1 MHz) and at 100 W input power is being discussed. The measurements have highlighted the places around the antenna where the field levels are high, from the perspective of safe exposure to electromagnetic radiation. Thus, it was found that on a line situated just beneath and parallel to the emitting antenna, the electric field strength may exceed the safety limit recommended for the population by ICNIRP guidelines. The magnetic field component however was lower than the limit in all considered cases.

articleTitle: Conceptual Model of a Variable Gap Magnet for a GeV Electron Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a conceptual model of a variable gap magnet aimed to work as spectrometer for electrons with high energy in GeV range. The magnet could be part of an experimental arrangement for e- energy spectra measurements for nuclear physics experiments. A one meter long magnet with a variable gap size, between 20 and 70 mm, has been designed. The magnet has a modular structure and will be fabricated using NdFeB magnets and iron yoke. The maximum magnetic flux density will be 1.58T. 3D numerical simulations of the magnetic field inside the gap were performed using the finite element method. The forces between poles were also computed in order to compensate them adequately. A special symmetric displacement system was conceived in order to adjust the gap size.

articleTitle: The Overvoltage Distribution across Transformer Windings in presence of Long Feeders
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This is a study presenting the impact of the long transmission lines or so-called feeders on the overvoltage distribution across power transformer windings. The overvoltage propagates along the power feeders until reaches a high voltage (HV) winding. The overvoltage is distributed across it. For the purpose of transient overvoltage evaluation, the HV winding model assumes distributed parameters. An equivalent circuit composed from series connected two-port elements substitutes the feeder. According to simulation results, the values of the line parameters play a significant role in determining the voltage across the HV winding. The strongly capacitive character of long feeders causes a larger voltage measured across the HV winding, compared to the line input. Moreover, the effective length of the transmission line is in direct correlation with the overvoltage amplitude across the HV winding. For this study, the model based upon lumped parameters and disk coils is suitable and provides appropriate information regarding the insulation requirements, as well. The signal, which emulated the commutation overvoltage, had a time variation closed to a step-up. All the numerical simulations from this paper have been performed running a software package called SYSEG (Symbolic State Equation Generation), prior developed by the authors.

articleTitle: Transient Response of Synchronous Generator to Faults on the Evacuation Overhead Line
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Normal operating conditions of synchronous generators are often perturbed by faults occurring on the evacuation overhead power line. Two events occurring on the evacuation overhead power line of Râul Mare Retezat Hydroelectric Power Plant are presented in the paper. It is about a two-phase short circuit and atmospheric discharges respectively. The monitoring was done using a system type Digital Modular Perturbograph (PDM). The first part of the paper is an overview of PDM devices and their characteristics that are described and afterwards the monitoring systems and practical use of PDM solutions are presented. Real cases of monitoring voltages and currents waveforms, their rms values and corresponding angles, are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Increasing the flexibility of trigeneration systems for a larger presence of renewables in the energy mix
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The presence of a large quota of the renewable in the energy mix might cause problems for large district cooling/heating system due to reduced operation times for the trigeneration/CHP plants. In order to insure the consumers' demand under these circumstances new, more flexible schemes are necessary for their design. Flexible district cooling systems might facilitate the integration of RES due to a more controlled approach to the cooling loads based on the presence of both absorption and compressor chillers in the operation. The study presented here shows that it is possible to use the two types of chillers in order to ensure a decrease of the power injected by the analysed system, thus allowing a higher quota of renewables in the energy mix. Even more, this power might be recovered very fast, and because of that the analysed trigeneration system might play an important role compensating the power drops of the renewable energies based plants.

articleTitle: Determination of the optimal operational energy zones and the mathematical models for wind power plants
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The present paper analyzes the operation of the wind energy system, consisting of a wind turbine, a synchronous generator with permanent magnets (SGPM) at time variant wind speeds. Capturing the maximum wind energy is a complex problem, difficult to solve in practice when the speed varies and over time and the mechanical inertia of the wind turbine is high, not allowing the generator speed to be optimally energy-efficient. The paper contains two distinct parts: 1st determining the power at the wind turbine for a given wind speed and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> periodically determination of the mathematical model of the wind turbine (MM-WT). Those two issues are solved by measuring the main functional sizes: mechanical angular speed, wind speed, and electric energy.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Socket for Smart Grid Applications using Ethernet over Power Lines and USB over IP technologies
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Smart grid modern implementation involves, besides alternative energy sources and various new electric appliances, the use of power line communication (PLC) technologies that allow utility extension towards multifunctionality and compactness. This paper proposes an implementation of such combined technologies: Ethernet over Powerlines (EoP) and USB over IP (USB/IP), in a proof-of-concept application, highlighting its advantages and drawbacks. The improvements of the application may be noted in the electricity infrastructure dimension, fast data transfer between a large range of peripherals, the reduction of electromagnetic interference and of the overall costs.

articleTitle: Improvement of Static Force Characteristic of AC Electromagnet Using DOE and FEM
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper presents a study on the improvement of static force characteristic of AC electromagnet using an optimization method based on design of numerical experiments performed with 2-D FEM in ANSYS software. The purpose of the study is to determine the size of the magnetic core and ring to ensure the best attraction force on the whole range of air gap, maintaining the overall dimensions of the device. The chosen design parameters are the rate of bottom core thickness, the rate of ring width and the rate of lateral core thickness. A device screening ensures that all three parameters are worth considering with a confidence level greater than 99%. The optimization problem was solved with the method by zooms, bringing an improvement of 5.68% of static characteristic. The magnetic force was determined based on the principle of virtual work, available in ANSYS software.

articleTitle: Regarding The Structural Analysis Of Silicone Rubber Obtained From Recycling Used Composite Electric Isolators
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Recycling and reusing materials for the development of new products has been an important subject for several years now, receiving the attention of the scientific community. Finding new processing methods and ways to improve the properties of the final materials is one trending subject. The paper analyses the morphological and structural characteristics of recovered silicone rubber from the envelope of used composite electrical insulators obtained using two different technological approaches. The samples obtained by injection and extrusion processes and then subjected to a vulcanization step, have been analyzed by means of Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in order to emphasize the character of the internal structure of the resulting materials. Our investigations show that the character of the samples obtained using the injection process is discontinuous, large cavities forming between the recovered rubber and the binder. However, the samples obtained by extrusion method have proved a uniform micro structural aspect, the internalizing of the recovered rubber granolas into the matrix being much higher. The conclusion shows that extrusion method is a better processing alternative for recovered silicone rubber from the envelope of used composite electrical insulators comparing to injection method, considering the micro structural characteristic of the resulting materials.

articleTitle: Electron diffusion in a sheared magnetic field and a stochastic electrostatic field revisited
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In our model the diffusion produced by a two-dimensional electrostatic stochastic field combined with a sheared magnetic field is analyzed numerically. We assumed, as in a lot of other papers, an isotropic spectrum of electrostatic fluctuations as a combination of a Gaussian one (for small wave-vectors) and a power-law k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> (for large wave-vectors). The running and asymptotic diffusion coefficients of electrons are obtained for physically relevant parameter values.

articleTitle: About the force localization exerted by the magnetic field on the ferrofluids. The Quincke’s effect
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In ferrohydrodynamics theory, the forces acting in the magnetic liquid are not always treated in a uniform manner. The present paper tries to give a consistent macroscopic view, pointing out the importance of the magnetostriction in the force Iocalization understanding. The magnetic liquid will be considered as a linear and nonconducting medium placed in a stationary (or quasistationary) field. In order to support the analytical study, a numerical analysis of the magnetic forces was made using FEM analysis and Matlab.

articleTitle: Advanced System for Testing of Three-Phase Induction Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This document presents an implementation of an advanced system that uses virtual instrumentation as the main component in the process of measurement and testing of three-phase induction machines. This approach permits the replacement of the old analog measurement techniques-which are still in use in the industry applications at some electrical motor testing benches, with the new advanced measurement system bench. This system bench is capable of Data Acquisition, Storage or Memorization on different media, Visualization of relevant Graphs, printing or distribution of Technical Reports or Analysis on-line or off-line in an automated manner. The general architecture of the proposed system is focused on the hardware components (transducers, conditioning, data acquisition, calculator) and software components (driver for the acquisition and manipulation-calculation of data, graphical presentation, other auxiliary programs and the ones to bring all the components together, virtual instruments). Some of the most important requirements of the international standards for testing three-phase induction motors are used: as general technical verification, determination of the windings resistance in DC, no-load testing; necessary virtual instruments can be easily further added to the system: locked rotor testing, running characteristics, temperature-rise test. This system would be very useful in industry applications in the domains of electrical machines for testing workbenches and design laboratories.

articleTitle: The computation of the kQ-product and properties of wireless power transfer systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient computation algorithm of the kQ-product, based on a generalized power transfer system. Giving an explicit definition for the kQ product- called also Figure of Merit (FoM), the inaccuracies of previous definitions have been over fulfilled. Based on the circuit theory, in the definition of the transfer quality factor, we prove that the kQ-product is very useful in the analysis and design of the load matching networks that are optimized for the maximum power transfer efficiency. In this way, the concept of the kQ-product is extended from just coupled coils to the general two-port systems.

articleTitle: Current issues in the management by dispatching of the operating regime and maneuvering with long electric lines in the national power system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The authors present in this paper the practical algorithms for calculating the voltage jump that occurs when connecting and disconnecting the long electric transmission lines from the power system. The overvoltages caused by the switching of these lines are also evaluated. These values must be taken into account by the managerial and operational staff to properly perform and coordinate manoeuvres. In the case study it was considered a (double circuit) 220 kV LEA overhead power line, for which the calculation algorithms for both no load and under load switching were customized, and two scenarios were studied, namely when the line is not compensated and when the line is compensated by a compensation coil.

Author Keywords: no load and under load switching
produced reactive power compensation by a compensation coil

articleTitle: Influence of the single-phase fault place on the neutral treatment system parameters in MV networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper aims to presents an analysis of the single-phase fault place on the neutral treatment system parameters in a 110kV / MV power distribution substation belongs to Energy Distribution Oltenia. The simulations were done for neutral system treated by a suppression coil connected straight to the internal services power transformer and the situations / variations of the parameters in both transient and stabilized conditions were studied in depth for 2 cases, namely: first when the single-phase fault was placed on the station bar and the second when the defect occurred at the end of a line fed from the power substation.

articleTitle: Electric Energy Reduction On Terraced House With Storage Battery Photovoltaic Plant- Real Case
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This study shows the real case of a terraced house with the installation of a photovoltaic system. The consumption of electricity has been reduced compared to the case without a photovoltaic system and further reduced with the addition of a storage battery system. The overall system has been analyzed in terms of costs and benefits for both cases compared to the start situation.

articleTitle: Modeling the Electromagnetic Field Distribution in a Shielded Enclosure Lined with Radio-Frequency Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents some aspects regarding the electromagnetic field distribution modeling within a shielded enclosure lined with radio-frequency absorbing materials. In order to model the distribution of the electromagnetic field inside the chamber, the CST Studio Suite<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> simulation software was used. A shielded enclosure model with 1 m side cubic geometry was built. It was desired to study its behavior at different frequencies in order to determine the shielding performance. Both the distribution of the field density on the surface of the enclosure's walls, and the field scattering at the interior and at the exterior of the enclosure were of interest. The chamber modeling was performed using radio-frequency absorbers in the frequency range 0 GHz - 10 GHz and the results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Using the Visual Basic Program for Modeling the Heat Transfer Through Glazed Building Elements
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: Existing models for describing phenomena of heat and mass transfer characteristic of the studies in the field of building thermotechnics and the installations related to the buildings have recently known a great magnitude. Given the complexity of modeling equations due to a large number of parameters that depend on the heat flow transmitted through glazing (windows), the authors have developed a calculation program in Visual Basic 6.0 for determining heat flow taking into account different types of exterior windows and different locations.

articleTitle: BLDC Controller for two-wheel vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive design of a controller for BLDC motor with maximal electric power around 1000W, using high-end components to provide high performance and more flexibility of the implemented algorithms at a low-level cost. The controller can drive a BLDC motor providing the possibility of rotating in both directions, create an electromagnetic brake and kinetic energy recovery system. The controller who has equipped a 500W electric scooter, and a 1000W electric motor cart and it proved to be reliable, performance and especially flexible and portable by parameterizing all the implemented software functions.

articleTitle: Power Converters for a HAPS Power Source Model
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: In this paper are presented the power converters used in a model of a power source on board of HAPS (High Altitude Pseudo-Satellites). The HAPS hybrid power source is provided with two conversion systems. The main power sources-photovoltaic panels, fuel cells and battery are conceived to provide 24 VDC. On board of HAPS there are used two standard voltages 28 VDC for low power loads and 270 VDC for high power loads-propulsion motor. In this purpose one use two conversion systems, one 24 VDC-28 VDC and one 24 VDC - 270 VDC, each one with stabilized output.

articleTitle: Computer Assisted Diagnosis of CED-CR2 Installations: Part II
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: To optimise the diagnosis process for Romanian railroad traffic safety installations a series of diagnosis charts were devised on which a diagnosis software package was created. In the first part of the paper we explain the installation's operation mode. At this point, the installation diagnosis is classically done at its sequence of operation steps, without detailing the actual failure cause. That is, only the schema where the failure appears is identified. In our work, through the diagnosis charts and the afferent software we can determine the actual failure cause. The software is written in Visual Basic. The maintenance staff using this software are quick and correct in reaching a decision about failure causes. Thus, train traffic delays caused by lengthy and problematic failure diagnosis is kept to a minimum. At the same time wrong maintenance decisions are eliminated and serious traffic events avoided.

articleTitle: Power Management on Board on HAPS
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: This paper presents an improved model of a HAPS power source and its simulations along one day cycle. This power source is a hybrid one composed by a photovoltaic panel, fuel cell and a battery provided for transition periods on sunrise and sunset. The simulations take into account the functioning periods of each source component and a source power management is simulated by switching the loads feeding between the source components. Numerical simulations were performed taking into account a variation of solar radiation corresponding to a summer day at a latitude about 45 degrees.

articleTitle: Automation of a Pneumatic Cement Transport Installation Using PLC
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Applied and Theoretical Electricity (ICATE)
abstract: The paper proposes the use of the PLC for the automation of a pneumatic cement transport installation. This type of installation is used inside cement plants as part of the cement production process and other products derived from it. PLCs control installation replaces a classical control installation, less reliable, with contacts and relays. For the control of the pneumatic transport of the cement was using Zelio PLC and one extension module, to increase the numbers of digital inputs and outputs, connected to PLC. The program was developed in function block diagram. Using PLC's controls, the installation has been considerably simplified, and troubleshoot installations are much easier.

articleTitle: Study of shielding effectiveness on spurious emissions of information systems by means of metallic and carbon powder screens
